en: Jātaka:
The Section of Five (Pañcakanipāta), Chapter on the Rich (Aḍḍhavagga)
5. The Kapota Jātaka:
"Now I am happy and healthy, free from thorns and having escaped my plight, O pigeon."
“I shall now bring satisfaction to my heart by eating this meat-vegetable with force.
“What kind of crane is she, with her crest?”
“Thief! You who leap over your grandfather! Come here, Balāka;
my friend the crow is fierce.”
“It is enough for you to laugh upon seeing me in such a state,
ravaged by the son of a cook.”
“Smeared with a paste of ground rice.
“You are well-bathed and well-anointed,
satisfied with food and drink;”
"And that lapis lazuli on your neck—
did it go to Kajaṅgalā?
"Whether it was a friend or an enemy, let it not concern you."
He went to Kajaṅgala;
having plucked feathers there,
they tied them around their necks as amulets.
“Will you receive it again, friend?
For such is your virtue;
for human enjoyments—”
“They shall enjoy their food together with the birds.
The fifth Jātaka, the Kapota-jātaka.
The third chapter, the Aḍḍha-vagga.
Its summary verse (uddāna) is as follows: Then Color, Virtuous Conduct, Modesty, Attainment,
Sumukha, Poison, Sāli, and the Best of Friends.
Then: Cakkapalāsa, Sarāja, Sato, Yava, Bālakapota, and Pañcadasa. Now, the summary of the sections (vagga-uddāna):
The praise of the Jina, endowed with incomparable qualities,
the twenty well-taught Jātaka stories,
and the holy life (brahmacariya) of the Great Seer—
"He spoke verses that were meaningful and well-phrased.
The Pañcaka-nipāta is finished.
